battle.name: 第二次拉丁戰爭
battle.theater: 拉齊奧南部阿爾巴山麓
battle.brief: 公元前340年，拉丁同盟聯合薩姆尼特與坎帕尼亞進攻羅馬，戰火自維蘇威火山燒到阿爾巴山麓，拉齊奧南部逐村爭奪。科林斯青銅盔是希臘式重裝的頂點，全正面開眼便於在密集中軍裡保持視線，卻擋不住橫劈；羅馬執政官靠軍團大隊的輪替與嚴整陣形把它戴活，最終在阿爾巴山決戰壓垮拉丁方陣。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 拉丁同盟方面：公元前四世紀中葉，羅馬以北的拉丁姆平原上分布著三十個拉丁城邦，組成以阿爾巴山朱庇特聖所為中心的邦聯，平日各邦自守，戰時由聯盟推舉的獨裁官統一指揮。開戰時聯軍統兵者為拉提尼烏斯，最後一役則由阿里西亞的維提烏斯執掌。聯軍以希臘式重裝步兵為主體，各邦按人口與財力出丁，另湊出拉丁騎兵；營壘、糧秣、指揮卻互不統一。羅馬方面：共和國的百人團大會與元老院選出兩名執政官，各領一軍；危急時另設獨裁官掌握最高指揮，公元前338年由卡米盧斯擔任。羅馬的兵源來自公民團體，軍制為每團四千人的軍團，再編為大隊與百人隊。聯軍盟友包括薩姆尼特人（由執政官蓋利烏斯·埃格納提烏斯統率）、坎帕尼亞人（以卡普阿與阿泰拉為主）、西迪基尼人、沃爾奇人與奧倫奇人；埃魁人與赫爾尼基人原本站在聯盟一邊，卻在關鍵時刻倒向羅馬。戰局背後還有山南高盧塞諾馬尼人向拉丁姆進逼的威脅，羅馬被迫在兩線應戰。
countriesEn: On the Latin League side: in the middle of the fourth century BC thirty Latin communities were spread across the Latian plain north of Rome, forming a league centred on the sanctuary of Jupiter on the Alban Mount. In peacetime each community kept its own armed force; in war the league appointed a dictator to command the coalition. The commander at the opening of the war was Latinius, and the man who led the coalition in the final battle was Vettius of Aricia. The coalition rested on Greek-style heavy infantry, with each community furnishing men in proportion to its population and wealth, plus a mounted contingent drawn from the Latin towns, while the camps, the supply and the command remained separate from one city to the next. On the Roman side: the Republic elected two consuls through the comitia and the senate, each commanding one army, and in a crisis appointed a dictator with supreme command — in 338 BC that office fell to Camillus. Rome drew its soldiers from the citizen body, and its army was organised into legions of four thousand men, subdivided further into maniples and centuries. The allies of the coalition included the Samnites, led by the consul Gellius Egnatius, the Campanians based on Capua and Atella, the Sidicini, the Volscians and the Auruncians; the Aequi and the Hernici stood on the Latin side at first, yet turned to Rome at the decisive moment. Behind the front lay a further danger, as the Cenomani Gauls moved down from Cisalpine Gaul against Latium and Rome was forced to fight on two fronts.
people: 羅馬方面的關鍵人物有三層。一是公元前338年出任獨裁官的馬爾庫斯·富里烏斯·卡米盧斯，他受命重新集結軍隊、指揮阿爾巴山之役，戰後主持拉丁城市的接管與結盟安排。二是同年當選的執政官蓋烏斯·波普利基烏斯與盧基烏斯·科爾奈利烏斯·西庇阿，前者以老練的策略統率大軍，後者是名門出身的青年將領，兩人各領一軍，是聯盟崩潰時的正面主力。三是公元前340年開戰之初的兩名執政官，據李維記載該年羅馬城內曾有瘟疫，其中一名執政官在任內病逝，另一人則在維蘇威戰敗後收拾殘軍、重整建制。拉丁一方有兩位名字被保留下來：拉提尼烏斯在首戰中統軍失利，維提烏斯在最後一役被俘，此人正是聯盟崩潰的關鍵人物。薩姆尼特的蓋利烏斯·埃格納提烏斯是全場最積極的策劃者，他主張把防禦戰拖成持久消耗，並利用山間狹隘設伏，差點讓羅馬主力全軍覆沒。羅馬方面的關鍵決定還包括執政官團拒絕出兵救援被埃魁人攻陷的佩杜姆，以及元老院堅持在敗後立即反攻、拒絕與聯盟議和。
peopleEn: The key Roman figures come in three layers. First, Marcus Furius Camillus, dictator in 338 BC, who was charged with regrouping the armies, directing the battle on the Algidus and then supervising the settlement of the Latin towns. Second, the consuls elected for that year, Gaius Poplicius and Lucius Cornelius Scipio: the older and more experienced Poplicius directed the mass of the army while the younger Scipio, a scion of a great house, led the other, and together they formed the striking force that broke the coalition. Third, the consuls of 340 BC, when the war opened: according to Livy a plague ran through the city that year, one of the two consuls died of it, and his colleague took charge of the wreckage, rallied the survivors and rebuilt the command structure after the defeat near Vesuvius. Two names survive on the Latin side: Latinius, who lost the opening action, and Vettius, taken prisoner in the last battle, the man whose fate was bound up with the collapse of the league. Gellius Egnatius of Samnium was the most energetic plotter of the whole campaign: he pressed for the defensive struggle to be turned into a war of attrition and used a narrow pass in the hills to ambush the Roman column, nearly destroying the Roman army. Among the crucial Roman decisions were the refusal of the consular colleagues to relieve Pedum, captured by the Aequi, and the senate's insistence on counter-attacking at once after the defeat instead of opening negotiations with the league.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯青銅盔，是本場戰爭的時代底色。公元前650年前後盛行的這款青銅盔有圓頂、闊檐與垂至口鼻的護鼻，面部只留眼前一道狹長的開口，觀察力極佳，卻幾乎擋不住側面砍來的刃；佩戴者一旦脫離隊形，就等於把頭頸交給敵人。波利比烏斯記述羅馬步兵裝備時指出，羅馬人此時仍近於希臘式：戴青銅盔、持縱橢圓大盾，用短矛與投槍，佩一柄希臘式短劍，頸上還掛一條深紅披風。薩姆尼特人則已用上更笨重的平面大盾、小腿甲與金屬胸甲，防護明顯高一級；坎帕尼亞與拉丁各邦的民兵多為自備的希臘式圓盾與科林斯盔；埃魁與沃爾奇民兵裝備簡陋，多半只有矛與投石。羅馬在圍攻拉丁營壘與拉丁城時使用壕溝、木柵、雲梯與投射器具，把營地按方形挖掘、四周掘壕，帳幕依百人隊分配；糧秣靠產糧區徵收與牛車、騾隊運輸，騎兵依財產資格自備坐騎，聯盟各邦的馬匹與糧食則各自籌措，協調極差。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card is the period signature of this war. The type, widespread from about 650 BC, had a domed crown, a broad brim and a nasal guard reaching down to the mouth, leaving only a narrow opening in front of the eyes: the field of view was excellent, but the head was almost unprotected against a blow from the side, and a man who stepped out of formation surrendered his skull to the enemy. When Polybius describes the equipment of the Roman infantry, he notes that the Romans still went essentially Greek: a bronze helmet, the long oval scutum, a short spear and the pilum, a Greek-style short sword, and a crimson cloak over the shoulders. The Samnites had already gone further, using a heavier flat shield, greaves and a metal cuirass, a clear edge in protection; the Campanian and Latin militias generally brought their own Greek-style round shields and Corinthian helmets, while the Aequi and Volscian levies were poorly equipped, with little more than spears and stones. When the Romans besieged the Latin camp and the Latin towns they dug trenches, erected palisades, used ladders and missile weapons, and laid out their camp in a square with a ditch on every side and tents allotted by century. Food and forage came by levy from the grain districts and by ox-cart and mule train; cavalrymen supplied their own horses according to the property census, whereas the league's horses and grain were raised separately by each city, which made co-ordination very poor.
tactics: 拉丁聯軍採希臘式密集方陣：重裝步兵以矛盾相接層層遮蔽，前排接戰後互推掩護，兩翼由各邦騎兵掩護，衝鋒前以投槍齊射拉開陣線。羅馬的戰術核心是軍團制下的大隊輪替：步兵以百人隊為單位編為縱深兩列的橫隊，擲槍之後以刀劍近身纏鬥，後排在前列力竭時頂上，使前線始終保有新力，同時保持嚴整的視線與腳步，這正是科林斯盔那種寬視野裝備得以發揮的前提。羅馬還善用拒絕側翼：陣形一翼後撤、另一翼保持原位進攻，用少量兵力黏住敵軍多數兵力，主力再由另一側迂迴合圍。公元前340年，薩姆尼特的埃格納提烏斯利用山間狹隘與峭壁設伏，讓羅馬縱隊在行軍途中遭側擊，軍營被奪，羅馬一度退保鄰近據點；兩名執政官重新集結後才扭轉局勢。公元前338年阿爾巴山之役，羅馬以兩支執政官軍加獨裁官軍的總優勢壓向聯軍本陣，赫爾尼基人臨陣倒戈使聯軍陣形裂開，羅馬乘勢集中兵力各個擊破，並乘勝攻破聯軍營寨。值得注意的一個反面教材是：羅馬軍拒絕為埃魁人攻陷的佩杜姆冒險攻城，卡米盧斯當眾斥責部下只像奴隸而不像士兵，寧可放棄救援也不肯破壞援軍只在外野作戰的規矩。
tacticsEn: The Latin coalition fought in the Greek manner, in a dense phalanx: heavy infantry stood shoulder to shoulder behind interlocking shields, the front rank pressed home and covered itself, the flanks were screened by cavalry raised from the individual cities, and the line opened with a volley of javelins. The core of Roman method lay in the rotation of maniples inside the legion: infantry were grouped in centuries and drawn up in two ranks in depth, hurling their pila and then closing in sword to sword, with the second rank stepping forward as the first grew tired, so that the front line always met the enemy with fresh troops, with order and footing intact — exactly the discipline that made a wide-field helmet such as the Corinthian usable at all. The Romans also practised the refused flank: one wing fell back and the other stayed in place to attack, pinning the bulk of the enemy with few men while the main force swung round from the other side. In 340 BC Egnatius used a narrow defile and steep rock to ambush the Roman column on the march, seizing the Roman camp and driving the survivors back into a nearby stronghold; only after the two consuls rallied their forces was the situation reversed. At the battle on the Algidus in 338 BC the Romans pressed the coalition's main body with the combined strength of the two consular armies and the dictator's army, the defection of the Hernici split the allied line, and the Romans concentrated their weight to defeat the broken parts in detail and then stormed the coalition camp. One instructive episode runs the other way: the Romans refused to march into the captured town of Pedum, and Camillus openly rebuked his men for behaving like slaves rather than soldiers, preferring to forgo the relief rather than break the rule that a field army does not enter towns for the sake of its own men.
data: 可用的數字主要來自波利比烏斯與李維，須留意古代數字常有誇大，但這場戰爭的制度性數字相對可靠。編制方面，波利比烏斯記載羅馬每個軍團為步兵四千人、騎兵三百人，一支執政官軍為步兵兩萬、騎兵一千二百；公元前338年羅馬出動兩名執政官各一軍，再加獨裁官卡米盧斯的一支，合計步兵約六萬的量級，騎兵總數在數千人上下。聯軍方面，各拉丁邦按人口出丁，總數與羅馬相去無幾，但指揮與補給分散。規模上，拉丁同盟有三十個城邦；戰爭歷時兩年，公元前340年開戰，公元前338年以阿爾巴山決戰收場，中間經維蘇威山之戰、一次因伏擊而生的慘敗，以及拉提尼烏斯營壘被攻破等戰鬥。距離上，羅馬城至決戰地阿爾加杜斯山（Monte Cavo）約三十公里，至維蘇威火山約三十五公里，維蘇威至海岸城市安提烏姆約二十五公里，拉丁盟各城多在三十公里圈內互相呼應。損失方面，古籍只說羅馬在狹隘地遭伏時死傷被俘甚眾，具體數目已不可考；李維另記公元前340年羅馬城內曾有瘟疫流行，執政官因此病逝一人，軍隊亦受牽連。
dataEn: The usable figures come mainly from Polybius and Livy, and ancient numbers need care, though the institutional data for this war are relatively reliable. As for organisation, Polybius records a Roman legion as four thousand foot and three hundred horse, and a consular army as twenty thousand foot and twelve hundred cavalry; in 338 BC Rome fielded one army for each of the two consuls and a third under the dictator Camillus, an infantry total of something like sixty thousand, with a few thousand cavalry in all. On the coalition side the Latin towns supplied men in numbers comparable to Rome's, but command and supply were scattered. In scale, the Latin League comprised thirty communities; the war lasted two years, opening in 340 BC and closing with the battle on the Algidus in 338 BC, with the fight by Vesuvius, a crushing defeat inflicted by the ambush, and the storming of Latinius's camp in between. As for distances, the city of Rome lies about thirty kilometres from the decisive ground on the Algidus (Monte Cavo), roughly thirty-five kilometres from Vesuvius, and Vesuvius stands some twenty-five kilometres from the coastal city of Antium, while the Latin towns lay close enough to support one another. On losses, the sources say only that the Romans lost heavily in killed and captured in the defile, and the precise figures cannot be recovered; Livy also records a plague in the city of Rome in 340 BC, which killed one of the consuls and affected the army.
cause: 這場戰爭是羅馬在拉丁姆的霸權與拉丁同盟的邦聯權益正面碰撞的結果。公元前358至357年的第一次拉丁戰爭，羅馬以執政官之力打敗拉丁聯盟；隔年聯盟在阿爾巴山一役反敗為勝，據說阿爾巴一名元老之子被殺，由此引發屠殺與仇恨，兩邊結下深仇。往後二十年，羅馬把手伸向拉丁同盟的外圍：公元前330年代蕩平沃爾奇人的城邑，公元前329年攻下阿布爾人控制的山口與鹽道，羅馬商路與盟邦網因此急速膨脹，聯盟城市紛紛改投羅馬，使聯盟感到自己的商路、盟市與宗教權威正被抽空。加上阿爾巴山朱庇特聖所的實際管治權早已落到羅馬人手上，聯盟只剩名分，經濟與軍事的雙重失衡促使拉丁各邦決定先發制人，公元前340年正式宣戰；他們拉攏薩姆尼特與坎帕尼亞，把一場拉丁權利的防衛戰升級為義大利中部同盟對羅馬的總體戰爭。
causeEn: This war was the result of Rome's hegemony in Latium colliding head-on with the league's federal rights. In the First Latin War of 358–357 BC Rome defeated the Latin League with consular armies; the following year the league reversed the result on the Alban Mount, where, according to the tradition, the son of an Alban elder was killed, setting off a massacre and a lasting feud. Over the next twenty years Rome reached out around the league's flanks: Volscian towns were reduced in the 330s BC, and in 329 BC Rome seized the passes and the salt road held by the Aequi, so that its trade routes and network of allies expanded rapidly and league cities began to turn to Rome one by one. The league felt its commerce, its markets and its religious authority being drained away, and the practical administration of the Alban sanctuary had already passed into Roman hands, leaving the confederation with nothing but a name. With its economy and its military position both deteriorating, the Latin towns decided to strike first and declared war in 340 BC. They brought in the Samnites and the Campanians, turning a defensive fight for Latin rights into a general war of the central Italian allies against Rome.
impact: 公元前338年之後，拉丁同盟的邦聯機構被解散：阿爾巴山的聯盟議會不再召開，阿爾巴長老與聖所的管治權歸羅馬，各拉丁城邦或取得羅馬公民權、或取得拉丁權利，成為羅馬的盟邦附庸。羅馬由此打開通往坎帕尼亞的大門，取得拉丁姆全部城邑與道路，把同盟體系改造成以自己為中心的附庸網，義大利半島的均勢從此傾斜。副作用同樣深遠：薩姆尼特人認為自己出力最多卻被排除在和約之外，羅馬又沒有歸還戰俘與戰利品，遂在公元前327年再挑起第二次薩姆尼特戰爭，坎帕尼亞從此捲入羅馬的擴張軌道。這場戰爭也推動了裝備變革：羅馬人面對薩姆尼特式平面大盾、小腿甲與胸甲的防護優勢，在公元前310年代逐步換裝，頭盔形制與投槍配重都隨之調整，武器防護在二十餘年內連續改寫。
impactEn: After 338 BC the federal structure of the Latin League was dismantled: the league's assembly no longer met on the Alban Mount, the office of Alban king and the guardianship of the sanctuary passed to Rome, and the Latin communities either received Roman citizenship or the status of Latin rights, becoming dependent allies of the Republic. Rome thus opened the road into Campania, took every town and road of Latium, and turned the league into a network of dependencies centred on itself, so that the balance of the Italian peninsula tipped decisively. The side effects were just as deep: the Samnites, who had borne much of the fighting, were excluded from the settlement, and Rome returned neither prisoners nor booty, so in 327 BC they raised the Second Samnite War and dragged Campania into Rome's orbit of expansion. The war also drove a change in equipment: confronted with the protection offered by Samnite flat shields, greaves and cuirasses, the Romans began to re-equip themselves in the 310s BC, reshaping their helmets and the balance of the pilum, so that the shape of armour was rewritten within a couple of decades.
result: 公元前338年，阿爾巴山麓的決戰決定了戰局：羅馬以兩支執政官軍與獨裁官軍合流兵力正面壓上，拉丁、沃爾奇與埃魁聯軍的方陣在正面攻勢下裂開，赫爾尼基人倒戈，聯軍崩潰，營寨被羅馬攻破，統帥維提烏斯被俘。聯盟各城隨即失去戰鬥意志，紛紛轉向羅馬，聯盟議會在阿爾巴山的最後一次會議被解散，拉丁同盟在法律與軍事上都不再存在。埃魁與赫爾尼基受制於羅馬，沃爾奇人退回山區成為附庸，拉丁姆落入羅馬的勢力範圍，羅馬隨後著手對付不肯罷手的薩姆尼特人，拉丁戰爭直接變成第二次薩姆尼特戰爭的前奏。整體而言，羅馬贏得了義大利中部的主導權，卻同時把一個更難纏的對手引到自己面前，勝利的代價在往後十年才完全顯現。
resultEn: The battle on the slopes of the Algidus in 338 BC settled the campaign. The Romans pressed the Latin, Volscian and Aequian line with the combined weight of two consular armies and the dictator's army; the phalanx of the coalition split under the frontal blow, the Hernici defected, the allied line broke, the camp was stormed and the commander Vettius was taken prisoner. The league's cities immediately lost their will to fight and turned to Rome one after another; the last assembly on the Alban Mount was dissolved, and the Latin League ceased to exist in law and in arms. The Aequi and the Hernici were brought under Roman control, the Volscians withdrew into the hills as subjects, and Latium fell within the Roman sphere of power. Rome then turned on the Samnites, who refused to stop, and the Latin War became the overture to the Second Samnite War. Overall Rome won control of central Italy, but in doing so dragged a more awkward opponent into the field, and the full price of that victory did not become visible for another ten years.
